en.title: Ability and skill
en.summary: Can and could express ability; be able to fills the missing forms.

paragraphs: English expresses ability with the modal verb can (present), could (past or conditional) and the phrase be able to. Modal verbs are followed by the base form of the verb and have no -s in the third person.

items: When I was five, I **could** read.
He **will be able to** drive next year.

blocks.html:
FormExample
positiveI can speak French.
negativeI cannot (can't) speak German.
questionCan you cook?
past abilityShe could run fast as a child.
past negativeHe couldn't open the door.
polite requestCould you help me?

paragraphs: Can and could have no infinitive, no future and no perfect forms. Use be able to for these. In the past, could describes general ability, while was able to describes a particular success: I was able to finish the exam yesterday (not: I could finish).

blocks.html:
FormExample
futureYou will be able to swim soon.
present perfectI have been able to relax.
after another verbI'd like to be able to dance.
one past successI was able to find a taxi.

paragraphs: To talk about a learned skill, use can or know how to: I can play the piano; She knows how to cook. With the senses and mental verbs, use can: I can hear it; I can see you; I can't remember.

items: Wrong: **She cans swim.** Right: **She can swim.**
Wrong: **I can to speak.** Right: **I can speak.**
Wrong: **I will can help.** Right: **I will be able to help.**
Wrong: **I could pass the exam yesterday.** (one event) Right: **I was able to pass.**
